headline: OpenAI launches GPT-5.6 family with speed and multi-agent work at its core
summary: The new GPT-5.6 family includes Sol, Terra, and Luna, offering tailored performance and cost. Sol can achieve up to 750 tokens per second for flagship capability.
details: OpenAI has officially launched the GPT-5.6 family, comprising Sol, Terra, and Luna, on June 26, 2026. This release focuses on delivering concrete speed improvements and advanced multi-agent work capabilities. The flagship GPT-5.6 Sol model can achieve up to 750 tokens per second with Cerebras support.

Speed is integrated with stronger reasoning, coding, biology, and cybersecurity features, along with new controls for complex tasks. This update provides a broader platform for developers and enterprises to balance latency, cost, and capability across various AI workflows.

The three-model family allows for tailored deployment: Sol for high-capability reasoning, Luna for maximum speed and efficiency, and Terra for a balanced approach. This distinction is crucial for teams building production systems with diverse requirements.

OpenAI plans API access for developers and integrations into ChatGPT, Codex, and AWS Bedrock. Organizations should consult official product materials for complete pricing schedules before making cost assumptions.

Higher throughput significantly improves interactive applications, reduces waiting times in tool-driven workflows, and makes longer outputs more practical. Multi-agent capabilities, currently in beta, enable complex, multi-step tasks like planning and coding assistance.

OpenAI is conducting ongoing safety evaluations in coordination with government bodies during the rollout. This highlights the need for governance, testing, and deployment boundaries as these more capable systems are adopted by enterprises.

headline: 7 States’ Water Systems Hit by Cyberattacks Likely Tied to Iran
summary: The FBI has warned that cyberattacks, initially reported in Minnesota, have now affected utilities in at least seven US states, potentially causing boil-water notices. A leaked memo and CISA advisory link these attacks to Iranian-affiliated hackers.
details: The FBI has warned that cyberattacks, initially reported across 30+ Minnesota water utilities, have now spread to at least seven US states. These attacks represent perhaps the broadest, most disruptive hacking campaign to ever target American industrial control systems.

The Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) advisory stated that some attacks disabled digital controls and 'resulted in boil-water notices,' suggesting potential water contamination. The FBI and EPA are actively working with affected utilities.

A leaked memo obtained by WIRED officially documents Iran's likely responsibility for these incidents, confirming earlier CISA advisories. Iranian-affiliated hackers are the leading suspect behind this widespread campaign.

Authorities urged utilities to immediately remove internet-connected programmable logic controllers from public access. They also recommended implementing strong passwords and setting up allow-lists for authorized device connections to enhance security.
